Elena / Neha —

Quick technical note on the latency SLO: achieving 95th <= 150ms consistently in EU for large prompt workloads requires either increased warm pool reservations or model quantization variants to reduce at-inference compute time. Tradeoffs: warm pools raise committed resource cost; quantized variants can reduce tail latency but may need evals for quality regressions.

We can commit to the 160–180ms range with +20% committed capacity off-the-shelf. If Finova wants 150ms 95th, we should schedule a short performance tuning window (2–4 weeks) and include an SLA amendment that lists fallback model variants during sustained degradation.

Adding our SLO appendix for reference.

— Rishi
Staff, Applied ML — Inference Performance
[Attachment: slo_tradeoffs.pdf]
